chapter: Trio years, the Sands and Armstrong recollections
title: World's Fair 1964 and drummer Keg Purnell
summary: Plays the Balcony at the 1964 World's Fair; Keg Purnell stayed eleven years.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: What place were you playing at the World's Fair?
A place called the Balcony in the Louisiana pavillon. It was Wonderful. Joe Jones was there on drums, Big Nick on sax.
(Inaudible) I had Keg Purnell with me, and Sy (inaudible). He stayed with me until he died. He was a wonderful drummer.
When did you first get him? What year?
I found him, when we went into Stuyvesant Casino and we were all gigging around, by myself.
That's the way I met Keg. When I went into the Frolic he stayed with me for eleven years.
I guess he's the best you ever had, next to A.G. Godley.
He was the best one I ever had, other than A.G. Godley; yeah.
He would have been great in the eight piece band. He was with Eddie Haywood all those years.
Yeah, he was with Eddie Haywood too.
You said Bob Carroll died; right?
